payload.claim: Amazfit Balance heart rate sensors were top-class in Live Science tests; costs $199
payload.quote: ✅ You want accurate tracking features: Its heart rate and body composition sensors were top-class in our tests.

payload.claim: Amazfit Balance accurately measured heart rate, breathing rate and HRV
payload.quote: This smartwatch accurately measured our heart rate, breathing rate, heart rate variability, and even body composition (!), and it never slid from our wrists or got in the way during intense workouts.

payload.claim: Balance has only non-essential extras (AI coach chatbot) behind a paywall
payload.quote: A few extras, such as the AI fitness coach chatbot, sit behind a paywall, but nothing essential does.

payload.claim: Xiaomi Band 7 Pro had the most accurate sleep tracking of budget bands tested
payload.quote: Its sleep tracking was the most accurate of any budget band I tested, reliably separating light, deep and REM sleep and catching the brief overnight wake-ups that other bands smoothed over.

payload.claim: Xiaomi Band 7 Pro sleep tracking is not accurate
Fitbit Air sleep stages and sleep score need Google Health Premium
payload.quote: Sleep stages and the nightly sleep score are reserved for Google Health Premium members, at $9.99 a month or $99 a year; without it, you see total sleep time, steps and resting heart rate and little else.

payload.claim: Fitbit Air is $99 and subscription-free for core features
payload.quote: At $99 and subscription-free for core features, the Fitbit Air is one of the best value screenless trackers available in 2026

payload.claim: Fitbit Air gives detailed sleep reports on par with top smartwatches
payload.quote: For a $99 wearable, the Fitbit Air provides detailed sleep reports on par with some of the best smartwatch models in 2026, with insights into your sleep duration, time spent in sleep cycles, restlessness, and daily sleep quality rating and score, also out of 100.

payload.claim: Garmin does not charge extra to access data on vivosmart 5
payload.quote: Plus, Garmin doesn’t charge extra to access all of your data and training assistance features, which is why it earns our top spot.

payload.claim: Garmin sleep data was the most consistent with lowest outliers (consistency, not accuracy vs reference)
payload.quote: Garmin produces the most consistent data – it shows the longest average sleep duration, the lowest variability, and very low outlier rates, making it the most reliable for long-term trend tracking.

payload.claim: Garmin had the highest outlier rates and widest variability in Terra benchmark
payload.quote: In Terra's benchmark of sleep data from thousands of Oura, Apple, Fitbit and Garmin users, Garmin produced the highest outlier rates and the widest night-to-night variability of the four platforms, which makes its long-term sleep trends the hardest to trust.

payload.claim: Apple recorded only 10.5% deep sleep vs ~18% others
payload.quote: Apple recorded an average of only 10.5% deep sleep, compared with nearly 18% for Garmin, Fitbit, and Oura.
Whoop is the clearest example: the strap itself comes free, but membership costs $199, $239 or $359 per year depending on tier, so over two years it costs more than anything else in this guide.

payload.claim: Inspire 3 needs Premium for detailed sleep data
payload.quote: In fact, you need to pay for the Premium subscription for quite a few insights—including detailed sleep data, wellness reports, and a Daily Readiness Score—which keeps the Inspire 3 from earning the top spot.

payload.claim: Popular Science lists accurate heart rate and sleep tracking as a vivosmart 5 pro
payload.quote: Accurate heart rate and sleep tracking

payload.claim: vivosmart 5 optical HR sensor is solid
payload.quote: Its optical heart-rate sensor is solid, and it tracks stress and respiration alongside sleep.
